findings.summary: A compact CPU neural thought-quality gate used five named submodules, online accepted/rejected outcomes, rule fallback, bounded consolidation training and SFT stabilization. Frozen code defines FEAT_DIM=42 while a nearby docstring still says 48; preserve the mismatch as stale documentation until a historical runtime receipt resolves it.

A March 14 audit found a degenerate always-accept pattern: ACC=0 and verdict about 0.9999. The rejection path had not written accepted=false outcomes. The saved training state was 0 negative and 960 positive examples. Repair added negative feedback on three suppression paths, reset the checkpoint and restarted from a small balanced buffer.

Frozen code retains 15% rule fallback even after maturity. After 5 consecutive rejects it raises fallback to at least 50%; after 10 it forces full rule fallback. The comment references a historical run with 19 consecutive rejects. This is a reusable collapse circuit-breaker pattern.
Training uses a bounded buffer and an 80 ms cycle budget. SFT health checking can restore anchored weights on critical drift, and checkpoints use temporary-file rename semantics.

Code-level inference: all named submodule losses are derived from the same final binary outcome. This weakly identifies the named internal semantics; separate labels, interventions or discrimination tests are required before interpreting the heads as distinct mechanisms.

The 0-negative/960-positive incident shows that learned-loop quality depends on complete outcome routing. Current learners need explicit terminal-outcome coverage, label provenance, class-balance telemetry and frozen evaluation before promotion.
A learned quality score may guide routing but does not itself authorize effects or establish external truth.

must_change: prove every terminal outcome path writes the intended label
separate mechanism claims from a shared binary teacher
evaluate candidate versus current on frozen data before promotion
keep learned gate below effect authority

branch_feedback.frank: Use learned quality gates only with deterministic fallback, complete outcome receipts and collapse tripwires.
branch_feedback.harness: Add the 0/960 label-collapse incident and repeated-reject blackout as historical regression tests; mutate feedback edges to verify detection.
branch_feedback.claycode: Represent terminal outcome identity, label provenance, fallback phase and restore state explicitly.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Persist learner label origin, support counts, model version, fallback activation and restore ancestry.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Separate model verdict edges from downstream outcome evidence and expose missing feedback edges as causal coverage gaps.
branch_feedback.gwt: If the gate modulates competition, broadcast provenance and fallback state with the signal.
branch_feedback.emergenz: Do not infer separate named mechanisms from heads trained on one shared binary target without interventions.
branch_feedback.hyperposition: Preserve alternative explanations for gate scores until causal tests discriminate them.
branch_feedback.clayresearch: Treat the failure as an anti-echo case where data-routing completeness dominated model architecture.

contradictions_preserved: FEAT_DIM=42 in runtime constant versus 48 in stale extractor docstring
named internal modules versus one shared binary training signal
coverage_reason: The Level-0 combined denominator is still NOT_FROZEN; this is a query-directed history/runtime shard, not exhaustive tree/history closure.
limitations: Historical checkpoint was not executed in this session; the 0/960 state is commit-recorded evidence.
The weak-identifiability point is a code-derived inference, not a representation-probing measurement.
promotion_boundary: Historical implementation and regression-test evidence only; no direct promotion of learned gate scores to independent truth or effect authority.
